label: Abortion Is A Double Standard
description: If God taking a life prematurely is an outrage, why is Hitchens taking one via abortion a moral right?

label: Atrocity From Divine Permission
description: The most brutal acts come from believing one has divine permission.

label: Beginning Implies Beginner
description: The Big Bang's beginning requires a transcendent beginner.

label: Consciousness Defies Chemistry
description: No materialist account explains why matter is conscious.

label: Constants Are Fine-Tuned
description: Life-permitting constants sit on a razor's edge, implying a tuner.

label: Design Need Not Be Optimal
description: Suboptimal design is still design; you can't judge it without the designer's purpose.

label: Designer Is Not Enough
description: Even a designer doesn't yield answered prayer, virgin birth, or resurrection.

label: Everyone Is An Atheist
description: Everyone disbelieves in thousands of gods; the theist must justify the one exception.

label: Fine-Tuning Cuts Both Ways
description: Accelerating dissipation and extinction suggest capricious or absent design.

label: Hitchens Borrows Morality
description: Hitchens must assume God's moral standard to argue against God.

label: Information Implies Mind
description: DNA's specified complexity could only come from a mind.

label: Materialism Defeats Reason
description: If thought is mere chemistry, reasoning cannot be trusted.

label: Miracles Fail Humes Test
description: A reported miracle is always less likely than the witness being mistaken.

label: No Virtue Unique To Believers
description: No moral act exists that only a believer could perform.

label: Objective Morality Needs God
description: Objective moral values require a moral lawgiver beyond humanity.

label: Religion Poisons Everything
description: Religion demands servile submission and yearns for the end of the world.

label: Vicarious Redemption Is Immoral
description: One may pay a debt but cannot assume another's moral responsibility.
